conclusion: CP27 is an exact one-shot OpenCL vecadd boundary, not general OpenCL support. Its sub-second direct wall time does not justify delaying normal Triton Python and model-operator coverage for an unconditional profiling checkpoint.
decision: Keep the exact image, ABI, geometry, trace, D2H mask, and one-submit admission fail closed. Proceed to normal Triton Python and then the model-required operator matrix. Open a profiling or optimization checkpoint only when retained evidence from a real operator, layer, or model shows a material bottleneck, and never promote a single timing observation into a simulator performance claim.
invalidated_assumptions: One hash-pinned vecadd proves arbitrary OpenCL images, kernels, or launch shapes.
One successful submit implies reusable multi-dispatch sessions, events, or asynchronous queues.
Correctness and operator coverage must wait for a microbenchmark optimization.
One host wall-time sample is a simulator performance or timing-model claim.
observation: The accepted image is exactly 5160 bytes with one SHA-256, an 88-byte kernarg, global/local sizes 1024/256, three 4096-byte buffers, one submit per context, four workgroups, sixteen waves, 448 instruction starts, 2048 reads, 1024 writes, 16 stores, C-only D2H, and CRC32C 3210199849. The retained direct run is about 0.94 seconds wall while gem5 reports about 0.07 host seconds.
question_or_symptom: Why does the accepted direct vecadd neither establish general OpenCL nor require profiling before normal Triton and model-operator coverage?
